leftEvidence.title: Fire falls and the people worship

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: Fire consumes the offerings, glory fills the house, and the people bow while musicians and sacrifices accompany the festival.
points.right: A collected letter recalls cloud and glory at the Temple, Solomon’s dedication, fire consuming sacrifice, and Moses’ earlier offering.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Priests cannot enter; Israel praises enduring covenant love and celebrates.
points.right: Solomon is placed inside a chain of remembered acts of divine acceptance.

payload.posture: Chronicles narrates fire and glory; 2 Maccabees recalls Solomon’s prayer and sacrifice alongside Moses.

rightEvidence.title: A later Temple memory recalls Solomon’s sacrifice

payload.tension: Later memory joins traditions that the earlier dedication account keeps in its own narrative frame.
payload.title: Dedication narrated and remembered
